coverage.reason: Policy background; creates no separate eligibility condition.
Establishes post-authorisation scope and home-supervision purpose; a separate supervision condition remains unresolved.
Heading identifies the subject, without enlarging the express fund definition.
Limits the listed measures to post-authorisation matters.
Separate operator-change measure expressly uses supervision; its condition is not automatically imported into item (ii).
Supplies the selected removal, home-compliance condition and feature/policy exceptions.
Notification alignment is separate from prior-approval removal; detailed duties are absent.
Identifies unavailable FAQs, forms and checklists needed for operational application.
Express commencement date governs the proposed predicate.
Preserves existing processing for specified pending applications; substantive effect is an explicit assumption.
Management-company heading does not itself impose a distinct approval condition.
Continued post-vetting and discretionary enforcement prevent equating approval removal with complete compliance.
Offers clarification through case officers; does not require consultation for every change.
Express circular-specific definition controls eligible fund status and domicile.
FAQ reference is relevant; its unavailable contents remain deferred.
Forms/checklists reference supports implementation; its unavailable contents remain deferred.

dimensions.explanation: The selected control concerns SFC prior approval of material investment changes in defined UCITS funds after authorisation. Operator changes, notification duties and post-vetting are distinct controls. Home-supervision purpose may qualify scope, but item (ii) does not expressly repeat that test.

The fund definition is express and limited to four named EU domiciles and UK-domiciled schemes authorised as UK UCITS. Materiality, novelty, complexity and potential local policy implications lack supplied assessment criteria.

Novel features, complex features or possible local policy implications each exclude the selected removal. Whether preservation of an existing application process also preserves substantive approval requirements remains unresolved.

Removal of a specified prior-approval requirement is limited relief. Continued post-vetting is stated affirmatively; follow-up enquiries and regulatory action are discretionary. Failure of removal eligibility does not establish the complete approval obligation.

The predicate uses 28 November 2025, including that date. Earlier receipt and pending status distinguish preserved applications. The publication date needed to reconcile 'immediate effect' and the precise pending-status assessment time are not supplied.
FAQs, forms/checklists, applicable home requirements and the existing process are unavailable. Opaque dependency identifiers cannot reliably be mapped to authorities merely by order.

questions: Do the relevant FAQs make home-regulator supervision a separate condition for item (ii), beyond compliance with home-jurisdiction requirements?
Does the transition preserve substantive approval requirements or only the existing processing procedure?
What criteria determine materiality, novel or complex features, and possible local policy implications?
What rules govern bundled changes, overlapping applications, amendments, withdrawal and resubmission?
What are the applicable home requirements, notification duties and existing approval rules, and which missing dependency identifier corresponds to each referenced resource?

assumptions: The express circular-specific definition is exhaustive for this measure; ordinary or broader uses of UCITS do not expand it.
Home-regulator supervision in the introduction describes the purpose; item (ii)'s express condition is home-jurisdiction compliance. Item (i)'s separate supervision condition is not imported.
The express Effective Date governs the introductory immediate-effect wording.
Pending application status is assessed at the Effective Date.
Preservation of the existing process excludes the pending application from this removal, without determining the full contents of that process.
The identified change is assessed as a whole; no severability rule is inferred.
This proposal remains subject to qualifications in unavailable referenced materials.

citations.quote: For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC.

readings.distinction: The refinement separates defined fund status, the kind of change and the regulator's selected control. A UCITS domiciled outside the enumerated jurisdictions is outside scope, rather than a failed in-scope eligibility case. A supervised operator change also does not become a material investment change merely because both receive streamlining. The tested rival would make introductory home supervision an additional item (ii) condition: it could exclude an otherwise home-compliant change lacking such supervision. That rival has some support in the introduction, but 'aim at' and the express supervision language in item (i), contrasted with item (ii)'s compliance language, do not establish a second executable condition. The strongest remaining uncertainty is whether the pending-application transition preserves substantive requirements. No comparable fact-bound counterexample was supplied; incomparability diagnostics do not establish disagreement on a shared case.

questions: Can an item (ii) change comply with home requirements while falling outside home-regulator supervision, and do the FAQs address that case?
Does 'existing approval or authorisation process' preserve the substantive prior-approval requirement for the selected pending application?
Which additional authorities determine whether prior approval is legally required when this limited removal is unavailable?
readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] The result answers whether a selected in-scope material investment change qualifies for item (ii)'s removal of SFC prior approval under the stated assumptions. Within scope, true means the assessment is on or after 28 November 2025, home requirements are met, no listed feature or policy exception applies, and no pre-effective pending application preserves the existing process. False means this removal is unavailable under this reading, not that approval is necessarily required or the fund is non-compliant. A false scope means this control supplies no determination. Unknown facts remain unknown. Notification, filing, post-vetting and overall compliance are not decided.
readings.subject: Eligibility for item (ii)'s prior-SFC-approval removal within the circular's defined UCITS scope
